text:
jordan: Heads up — we're seeing partial GPU pod evictions in eu-central-1 since 08:12 UTC. p50 +120ms, p95 ~1.2s, 503 spike to 2.8% across the model fleet. Control plane shows 2 worker pools in that region reporting OOM/evict.
maria: Ack. Are these preemptions or node-level network flaps? any node alerts in the pool logs? :eyes:
ops-bot: Alert: eu-central-1/gpu-pool-3 - 12 pod evictions in 18m; avg GPU utilization 89%; node-restarts 4; recent kernel OOM events detected. See /alerts/1796507777
jordan: Kernel OOMs per ops-bot. My quick mitigation thought: soft GSLB reroute ~20% to na-west so we relieve pressure and give pods time to stabilize. Keep weight TTL low for rollback. Prefer gradual increments.
cheng: 20% seems OK but be mindful of KV-cache cold-start — moving traffic will cause many requests to miss prefix/KV caches and spike GPU memory & latency in the target region. Plan warmers or reduce context size for redirected sessions.
anya: +1 on staged rollouts. Proposed plan:
1) shift 5% every 3 minutes up to 20%
2) set GSLB TTL -> 15s
3) start synthetic warmers for top 10 prompts in na-west
4) monitor p95/errors; rollback if 503 > 1% or p95 > 750ms for 5m
sam: Cost note — na-west reserved capacity is lower right now but if we overflow to on-demand/spot we might see a cost bump. Check capacity in na-west dedicated pool before shifting too much.
kevin: We also have na-east warm capacity with cheaper spot mix. Could do split: 12%->na-west, 8%->na-east. But na-east has higher network egress to EU users (latency tradeoff).
maria: If we do multi-target, ensure smart-routing policy sends sticky sessions (long context / active KV entries) back to eu if possible. Otherwise session rebuilds will blow up token costs and latency.
jordan: Good point. We'll route by cookie/session header: long-context -> eu; short/simple -> fallback regions. Also lower model max_seq for fallbacks to reduce GPU mem.
cheng: I'll kick off warmers. Warming script (runs in infra-tools):
```
./warmer --region na-west --model redwood-xl --prompts-file top_prompts_10.json --qps 10 --duration 600
```
Start after we bump weight to 5%.
jordan: Executing staged GSLB change now (dry-run first). Command to change weights via control plane API:
```
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/gslb/weights \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"changes":[{"from":"eu-central-1","to":"na-west","percent":5}],"dry_run":true}'
```
kevin: Also set healthcheck sensitivity to avoid flapping: increase consecutive healthy threshold to 3 before considering a region healthy after changes.
maria: I'll watch billing/quotas in parallel. If na-west scales to on-demand, we need to cap at 15% to avoid high spend.
jordan: Dry-run succeeded. Rolling 5% -> na-west now. ops-bot, start warming when the weight is live.
ops-bot: GSLB change applied: eu-central-1 -> na-west 5% (non-dry-run). Monitoring: now p95 eu -> 1.05s, errors down to 1.9%. Warmer queued for na-west.
cheng: Warmer started (PID 3421). Initial cache hit rate in na-west is 0.6% (expected). Will post updates every 60s.
sam: Checked na-west capacity: 120 available reserved slots; autoscaler will spin-up up to 40 on-demand if needed. Cost alert threshold set at 30 on-demand.
anya: Observability checklist:
- p50/p95 per-region
- 503/error-rate global + per-route
- KV cache miss ratio
- model memory pressure
I'll post a dashboard link: /dashboards/gslb-shift/1796507777
jordan: Moving to 10% now (5% -> 10%). Keep TTL=15s, health threshold=3, rollback criteria active. If anyone sees unexpected behavior, shout here and I’ll revert to 5%.
kevin: Seeing a transient p99 spike in na-west for long-context sessions. Could be cold KVs. Suggest throttling long-context reroutes for next step.
maria: pausing further scale to 15% until p99 stabilizes. Cost OK so far.
ops-bot: Update: after 10% reroute, global 503 -> 1.1%, eu-central error rate 1.2% (down from 2.8%). No autoscaler triggers yet in na-west.
jordan: Thanks all. Hold at 10% for 20m while warmers continue and SRE/infra investigate OOM root cause. Plan follow-up: if eu node OOMs stop, we can roll back traffic gradually; if they continue, evaluate node kernel patch + replace node image. Ending here for now — will update thread with root cause analysis once available. :white_check_mark:
